newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul chipmaker shares little affected by EU move.
newsitem.headline: Seoul chipmaker shares little affected by EU move.

text.p: Shares of South Korean chipmakers were seen little affected by the European Union's move to set minimum prices on memory chip imports from Japan and South Korea, brokers said.
Shares of the country's three memory chip makers fell in late Tuesday trading, but brokers said the declines were in line with the overall market weakness.
Samsung Electronics Co, the world's largest DRAM maker, fell 0.76 percent or 400 won to 52,400, after hitting an intraday low of 51,800.
LG Semicon Co was down 3.46 percent or 900 won to 25,100 and Hyundai Electronics Industries Co lost 0.93 percent or 300 won to 32,000.
The European Commission said on Monday it was reintroducing minimum prices on DRAM computer chips originating in Japan and South Korea.
It did not say what the minimum prices would be.
"I don't see any direct impact on the three firms' share prices. The falls were due to the gloomy mood on the overall market," said Lee Gyu-bum, an analyst at Hyundai Securities.
Moon Jong-geon of LG Securities agreed. "The move itself doesn't mean chipmakers will be seriously damaged, so investors remain calm."
The Seoul stock market fell on Tuesday, hit by increasing market interest rates and poor economic fundamentals. By late afternoon, the composite index shed 1.6 percent, or 10.69 points, to 656.66.
